quotes.text: Raw network response codes for card payments vary by card network. The following tables describe each network’s codes.
`A1` | Soft decline (electronic commerce only), 3DS with challenge required.
`60` | Cardholder authentication required; repeat authorization with PIN.

old_evidence.text: Network decline codes are typically alphanumeric error codes that indicate a reason for a payment decline.

findings: The November same-URL capture inserts a Card Payments section with 13 named raw-response-code tables between the Bacs and Cash App Pay tables (new 62-815). It covers Visa, Cartes Bancaires, Eftpos AU, UnionPay, CAFIS JCB, Cybersource, Girocard, JCB International, Mastercard, American Express, Discover, NYCE and Everlink (Interac). The May capture has only seven payment-method groupings and no card section (old 10-119). Existing source summary lines 13-25 are now incomplete if used as a description of the new page; add a clear card-network route and retain the older seven-method snapshot qualification.

The new card tables have only Raw network code and Explanation columns (new 62-815), unlike the bank debit and Cash App Pay tables which map raw codes to Stripe decline/failure codes and often next steps (new 11-60, 817-875; old 10-119). Do not convert a Visa, Cartes Bancaires, Mastercard or other raw card code to a specific Stripe decline code or advice_code from this capture alone.

Card code meanings are network-specific, not interchangeable: Visa 05 is 'Don’t honor' (new 74), UnionPay 05 is 'ID certification fails' (new 281), and Mastercard rows combine a raw code with MAC values whose implications differ, including retry-later and do-not-retry variants (new 575-586). A user searching for card response codes now needs this source via stripe-index and the stripe-declines concept's Network Decline Codes section, with code-table detail left in raw.

The older ACH, AU BECS, Bacs, Cash App Pay, NZ BECS, Canada PAD and SEPA rows and response descriptions remain substantively present (old 10-119; new 11-60, 817-875). The large diff repeats them because table separator/padding rendering changed (diff 3-97, 853-955); no mapped bank debit code change is evident in those compared rows.

The existing source's Common Failure Codes table at lines 29-36 describes typical resolutions across methods. Keep those as summaries of the bank-debit examples, not universal card-network advice. Its generic_could_not_process 'Contact Stripe Support' row is too broad for old/new AU BECS and Bacs rows that supply only 'The payment failed' (old 32, 43, 50; new 33, 44, 51); SEPA's generic code row specifically says contact Support (old 111; new 867).
substantive_changes: A large card-payment raw network response reference is newly captured, with 13 named tables and network-specific code descriptions but no Stripe decline-code crosswalk or universal retry instruction (new 62-815; absent in old 10-119).
historical_claims_to_preserve: Keep the May seven-method bank-debit/Cash App Pay capture as dated evidence; its rows remain available in the November page (old 10-119; new 11-60, 817-875).
Preserve payment-method and network identity when using a raw code; the same code string can mean different things in different card tables (new 66-815).

Preserve mandate collection, new account details and contact-customer actions as method-specific guidance from the bank debit tables, not card-network instructions (old 10-59, 78-119; new 11-60, 834-875).
conflicts: Current source summary line 13 says the page maps raw network/bank decline codes to Stripe decline codes for seven payment methods; the November capture adds card raw-code explanation tables without Stripe decline-code mapping (new 62-815), so that description no longer fits the whole same-URL page.

Current source Common Failure Codes line 36 generalizes Contact Stripe Support for generic_could_not_process, while the captured AU BECS/Bacs rows offer no such next step (old 32, 43, 50; new 33, 44, 51).
unresolved_questions: The capture does not establish a runtime mapping from each raw card network code to a Stripe decline_code or advice_code, nor whether a specific issuer, network or merchant will return any listed code.
The presence of a raw network code in a table is not evidence that a bank authorization, capture, refund or settlement occurred in this review.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/declines/network-codes, the November capture adds card-payment raw response tables for 13 named networks or processors (new lines 62-815), which the May capture lacked between its Bacs and Cash App Pay sections (old lines 35-76). [[source-stripe-network-decline-codes]] currently describes only seven payment-method mappings, so it needs a dated scope update and card-table locator. The older bank debit and Cash App Pay mappings remain substantively present (old lines 10-119; new lines 11-60 and 817-875).
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/declines/network-codes, [[source-stripe-network-decline-codes]] should distinguish card raw-code explanations from bank debit tables that map codes to Stripe failure codes and next steps. The new card section uses two columns and warns codes vary by network (new lines 62-68); the prior bank tables map ACH R05-family codes and SEPA MD01 to debit_not_authorized (old lines 17 and 113; new lines 18 and 869). A raw card code alone does not prove a Stripe decline_code, retry decision or completed bank transaction.
